neighbours.label: the abstract noun inside a formal purpose or ground adjunct of the shape 'as a mark/sign/token of N' or 'as punishment/compensation for N', not the same ground expressed as a clause
fire: The flags were lowered as a sign of mourning for the victims.
The medal was given as a reward for forty years of service.
Players wore black armbands as a tribute to their former coach.
The fee was withheld as compensation for the damaged crates.
Workers walked out as a gesture of solidarity with the dockers.
He was suspended as punishment for falsifying the timesheets.
The gift was offered as a token of gratitude to the host family.
The gates were closed as a precaution against further flooding.
quiet: The flags were lowered because the whole town was mourning the victims.
The medal was given when he retired after forty years of service.
Players wore black armbands and remembered their former coach.
The fee was withheld until the damaged crates were replaced.
Workers walked out and the dockers cheered them from the gate.
He was suspended after falsifying the timesheets.
The gift was offered to the host family on the last evening.
The gates were closed before the river rose any further.

predictions: Fires on the noun naming the social motive inside an as-adjunct; rewriting the same ground as a because/after clause should drop it.
short: noun in an 'as a mark of N' adjunct
notes: Probe: 'as a mark of respect' 0.616, 'as punishment for' 0.560, vest|ig|ial 0.337, 'radius of curvature' 0.124, 'honoring ... with a plaque' 0.123, prisoner's dilemma 0.031, and plain twins 0.020-0.077. The frame, not the noun alone, is the claim: every near miss keeps the motive but drops the as-adjunct.
